final_answer:
RUNX1 chromatin occupancy increases and redistributes strongly after CBFβ-SMMHC inhibition with AI-10-49. In the provided RUNX1 ChIP-seq narrowPeak files, called RUNX1 peaks rose from 1,329 in DMSO to 9,169 after AI-10-49. Merging both conditions produced 9,266 consensus RUNX1 intervals: 7,950 were AI-only, 617 were shared but at least 2-fold higher in AI-10-49, 599 were shared with <2-fold change, 97 were DMSO-only, and only 3 were shared but at least 2-fold lower in AI-10-49. Thus, 8,567 sites gained or strengthened RUNX1 occupancy versus only 100 sites that were lost or weakened.

The gained RUNX1 sites were not randomly distributed: AI-only sites were enriched at promoters (3,307 promoter-proximal sites; promoter enrichment OR=1.51, FDR=6.08e-5 versus stable shared RUNX1 peaks). H3K27ac context showed that most RUNX1 sites overlapped active chromatin marks, but RUNX1 gain was not accompanied by uniform H3K27ac gain (median H3K27ac log2FC was -0.16 at AI-only RUNX1 sites and -0.27 at shared AI-higher sites). Around the MYC ±2 Mb regulatory domain, all 13 detected RUNX1 consensus peaks were AI-only or AI-higher, including a MYC-promoter peak and multiple distal sites.

Overall, AI-10-49 does not cause broad RUNX1 eviction; it is associated with a large net gain/reprogramming of RUNX1 occupancy, especially at promoter-proximal regulatory regions, with MYC-locus remodeling as a plausible mechanistic target. Because only one narrowPeak file per condition was available, these results are descriptive and should be validated with replicate, read-count-based ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN and matched expression assays.
